answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when independent audits uncover coordinated fraud. A newcomer cannot gain influence merely by spawning identities: every sybil must lock fresh capital, while shared control or copied behavior can trigger a correlated penalty. The stake might be a relic credential recorded on-chain; a violet mark from an audit can expose a forge attempt and put the bond at risk. The attacker pays in capital and time, and loses funds if caught.
